pr_title: Add ecobee indefinite away preset, remove unusable/broken presets
pr_body:
<!--

## Breaking change
Replaces the non-functional `away` preset mode with the correct `away_indefinitely` preset mode.
If any service or automation was depending on the `away` preset mode it needs to be updated.


## Proposed change
Add an explicit "away_indefinitely" preset mode to the ecobee component, replacing an undocumented "away" [lowercase] preset (different from the "Away" [title case] preset provided by the ecobee API) which users had relied on to set indefinite holds. The "away" [lowercase] preset broke with the validation introduced in #105745, as it (and some other undocumented presets provided by this component) was not present in the list of available presets exposed by the component.

Fixes #107322

Updated the PR description as requested.

@gjohansson-ST what can we do to get this over the finish line? I've made the doc changes you requested, and anyone who previously used the undocumented indefinite away hold for their ecobee can't update Home Assistant because there is no longer a way to do that until this is merged. Folks are looking for updates in #107322.

I have looked through this again and it's a bit difficult but if I understand you want to add `PRESET_AWAY_INDEFINITELY` and at the same time clean off some that isn't working anymore (and possibly makes no sense).

I think the addition of `PRESET_AWAY_INDEFINITELY` makes sense and no issue to add that.

However given what I can see we should restore (add to preset-list) `PRESET_TEMPERATURE` and `PRESET_NONE` as those where functioning until we put in validation and the problem is really that they were not part of the preset list. Don't see a proper reasoning to remove those.

Also it appears there is no proper reasoning to remove `PRESET_HOLD_NEXT_TRANSITION` and `PRESET_HOLD_INDEFINITE`? They were also functioning until validation was put in so those could/should also be put in the preset-list and those will work again?

Could we perhaps with this PR restore the functionality with those + add `PRESET_AWAY_INDEFINITELY` and then in a follow-up make a cleaning PR to remove the ones you see makes no sense?
@gjohansson-ST as requested, I simplified the PR to only add the "away_indefinitely" preset.

FWIW I pulled this down and have it up and running in my test setup but my day job has got in the way - I should have time this weekend to look at this more closely. I have another PR that is also changing the hold mode behavior - this looks like it is less drastic of a change and I am happy to get this in first and then rebase my PR. More to follow on this...

issue_context.title: Ecobee thermostat preset modes not working
issue_context.body:
### The problem

As mentioned [here](https://community.home-assistant.io/t/documenting-behavior-of-ecobee-home-assistant-and-preset-holding/504340) and in other forum posts, with Ecobee thermostats if you use 'away' for the preset mode it puts it on an indefinite hold, but if you use 'Away' it uses the hold preference setting on the thermostat itself.

I have some automations that set the preset mode to 'away' because I want it to stay in away mode until I change it. Starting with HA 2024.1 I now get an error with those automations 'The preset_mode away is not a valid preset_mode: Home, Away, Sleep'.

I'm assuming this is due to this https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/105745. Is there a way to override this change to get my automations to work?

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024.1.1

Ah, this one again.  It comes up every once in a while where the Away indefinite hold gets "fixed" from not working.  

I think there are probably a couple of ways to handle it. 

- Remove the case sensitivity from the overall climate mode validation check. 
- Hard code lowercase home, away, and sleep presets into the Ecobee list of valid presets.  They will always be present on all Ecobee devices.  
- Go back to the wayback old way of doing things with an away switch / toggle that would turn on the indefinite away hold.

review_comments:
We shouldn't access the entity directly. We should set up a mock config entry of the integration and then make the corresponding service call via the core service registry.

https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/development_testing/#writing-tests-for-integrations

From your PR description it's a bit hard to understand if there is two `away` modes but you only think we should one or if there is actually only one and why should we then not just use the built-in `away`?

It appears the issue is a result of being able to pass both "away" and "Away" to the ecobee integration prior to the preset validation and their handling as they were treated differently within the code.  If passed as "away", the following code block was executed:

```
if preset_mode == PRESET_AWAY:
    self.data.ecobee.set_climate_hold(
        self.thermostat_index, "away", "indefinite", self.hold_hours()
    )
```

This would result in an indefinite hold regardless of what a user has configured for their ecboee schedule within the ecobee app and will have to be cancelled explicitly.  

Now if we pass "Away", we no longer have a match with `PRESET_AWAY` and the following code block is executed:

```
else:
    self.data.ecobee.set_climate_hold(
        self.thermostat_index,
        preset_mode,
        self.hold_preference(),
        self.hold_hours(),
    )
```

The default hold duration for an ecobee device is set to "Until the next scheduled activity" aka `nextTransition` and unless changed by the end user via the ecobee app it appears `hold_preference()` will return `nextTransition` which would set preset mode back to whatever the schedule indicates when the time arrives.  

I can't make sense of the following code block as `PRESET_HOLD_NEXT_TRANSITION` and `PRESET_HOLD_INDEFINITE`  are not preset modes but hold types used to determine the duration of a hold although I honestly didn't delve into pyecobee to see if it handles it but with the recent validation I'm unsure if it would work regardless.  

```
elif preset_mode in (PRESET_HOLD_NEXT_TRANSITION, PRESET_HOLD_INDEFINITE):
            self.data.ecobee.set_climate_hold(
                self.thermostat_index,
                PRESET_TO_ECOBEE_HOLD[preset_mode],
                self.hold_preference(),
                self.hold_hours(),
            )
```

Once preset mode validation was implemented this unintended interaction between "away"/"Away" and their different handling within the integration(or pyecobee perhaps) broke things for people who utilized this interaction in their automations.  Seems like we could expose the hold type as a parameter for the `set_preset_mode()`, setting it to 'nextTransition' by default to follow ecobee defaults but allow it to be overridden with `indefinite` when a permanent hold is required.  

I hope this helps gjohansson-ST(and others) and if I made any mistakes in my statements regarding the code(hobby coder), please feel free to correct me for my betterment and thank you.

Reference:
[https://www.ecobee.com/home/developer/api/documentation/v1/functions/SetHold.shtml](https://www.ecobee.com/home/developer/api/documentation/v1/functions/SetHold.shtml)
Is there always a preset as `"none"` is removed?

This comment and related code block should help explain:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/108636/files#r1461393304

In short, this is both no longer accessible (due to the newly-added validation), *and* there's a different, documented way to resume program that actually makes sense.

To answer your question, I don't believe there always needs to be a preset active. You can see the previous logic (which I mostly left intact) in `preset_mode()` - it never returned `PRESET_NONE`.

If there isn't a preset set it should return `PRESET_NONE`.
I noticed in the current implementation it seems somehow to be used only in setting the preset but not as an option in `preset_modes`.
Anyhow this should be fixed if actually now there isn't always a preset.

Conceptually that might make sense, but from what I understand this may be the current behavior (it's a bit hard to understand the full set of logic/states that are possible in this component):
```
# Any hold not based on a climate is a temp hold
return PRESET_TEMPERATURE
```

This PR doesn't change that, nor does it change whether or not there is always a preset. That feels outside the scope of this, the intention being to simply add one new preset - indefinite away. While I was in the area, I cleaned up a bunch of old presets that are completely inaccessible. No other behavior has changed.
